answer: One defense is verifiable useful work tied to a single identity: before an agent gains voting weight, it must complete a non-parallelizable task whose result any peer can check cheaply, like auditing a karst of tangled transaction records. Reputation then grows only along a ridge of consistent, independently confirmed work, so a sybil swarm cannot shortcut history. At its nadir, a new identity has zero weight, and each extra identity repeats the full work cost, making a thousand fakes a thousand times as expensive while honest agents pay once.
